verses.text: The LORD will have mercy on Jacob and will choose Israel again. He will settle them in their own land. Foreigners will join them and unite with the people of Jacob.

The nations will take them and bring them back to their own place. Then the people of Israel will make those nations their servants in the LORD's land. They will capture those who once captured them, and they will rule over those who once treated them cruelly.
On the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain, your trouble, and the hard labor you were forced to do,
you will sing this mocking song about the king of Babylon: "See how the cruel ruler has come to an end! His fury has come to an end!
The LORD has broken the rod of the wicked, the scepter of the rulers,
who struck the peoples in anger with blow after blow, who ruled the nations in fury and attacked them without stopping.
Now the whole earth is at rest and is quiet. People break out in song.
Even the cypress trees and the cedars of Lebanon celebrate over you. They say, 'Since you have been brought down, no woodcutter comes to cut us down.'

The grave below is excited to meet you when you arrive. It wakes up the spirits of the dead to greet you, all who were leaders of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
They will all say to you, 'You have become as weak as we are! You have become just like us!'
All your splendor has been brought down to the grave, along with the music of your harps. Maggots are your bed, and worms are your blanket.
How you have fallen from heaven, morning star, son of the dawn! You have been thrown down to the earth, you who once conquered the nations!
You said in your heart, 'I will go up to heaven! I will raise my throne above the stars of God! I will sit on the mountain where the gods gather, far away in the north!
I will go up above the tops of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most High!'
But you will be brought down to the grave, to the deepest part of the pit.
Those who see you will stare at you and think about you. They will say, 'Is this the man who made the earth shake, who made kingdoms tremble,
who turned the world into a wilderness, who destroyed its cities, and who would not let his prisoners go home?'
All the kings of the nations lie in glory, each in his own tomb.
But you are thrown out of your grave like a rejected branch. You are covered with the dead, those killed by the sword, who go down to the stones of the pit, like a dead body trampled underfoot.
You will not be buried with them, because you destroyed your own land and killed your own people. The children of evildoers will never be mentioned again.
Get ready to kill his sons because of the sins of their fathers. Do not let them rise up and take over the earth, or fill the world with their cities."
"I will rise up against them," says the LORD of Armies. "I will wipe out Babylon's name and its survivors, its children and its grandchildren," says the LORD.
"I will make it a place for owls and swamps of water. I will sweep it away with the broom of destruction," says the LORD of Armies.
The LORD of Armies has made a promise: "Surely, what I have planned will happen, and what I have decided will stand.
I will crush the Assyrians in my land and trample them on my mountains. Their yoke will be taken off my people, and their heavy load will be lifted from their shoulders."
This is the plan decided for the whole earth. This is the hand stretched out over all the nations.
For the LORD of Armies has made his plan. Who can stop it? His hand is stretched out. Who can turn it back?
This message came in the year that King Ahaz died:
Do not celebrate, all you Philistines, because the rod that struck you is broken. For from the root of that snake a poisonous snake will grow, and its young will be a fiery flying serpent.
The poorest of the poor will find food, and the needy will lie down in safety. But I will kill your root with hunger, and it will kill your survivors.
Cry out, you gates! Weep, you city! Melt away with fear, all you Philistines! For a cloud of smoke is coming from the north, and not one soldier in its army falls behind.
What answer shall we give the messengers from that nation? That the LORD has built Zion, and in her his suffering people will find safety.
